ordered_diagnoses: periapical cyst associated with a previously endodontically treated tooth

facts.raw_span: pain and slight mobility of the mandibular right second premolar and first molar
tender percussion of both teeth
no erythema, ulceration, or warmth
bony‐hard consistency of the buccal and lingual cortices
mucosal integrity was intact
unilocular radiolucent lesion engulfing the apices of the right mandibular second premolar and a previously endodontically treated first molar
irregular shape was atypical for routine periapical cysts or granulomas
buccolingual expansion with almost complete obliteration of the lingual cortex
measuring approximately 23.4 × 14.2 × 6.6 mm
odontogenic keratocyst, radicular cyst, and unicystic ameloblastoma

concepts.why: The presence of a unilocular radiolucent lesion with an irregular shape and buccolingual expansion is consistent with an odontogenic keratocyst, which is supported by the radiographic findings.
The location of the radiolucent lesion at the apex of the tooth and its association with a previously endodontically treated tooth are consistent with a radicular cyst.
The presence of a unilocular radiolucent lesion with buccolingual expansion and the absence of signs of malignancy are consistent with a unicystic ameloblastoma.
The presence of tender teeth and the absence of signs of infection or malignancy are consistent with a periapical granuloma.
